title: Egg omelet with cheese, tomatoes, and dark‑green vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet prepared with creamy cheese, fresh tomatoes, and dark‑green vegetables such as spinach or broccoli, with a modest amount of added fat for flavor and texture. The dish is rich in protein, B‑vitamins, vitamin C, vitamin K, and minerals like calcium, iron, and potassium.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most nutrient‑dense foods, containing all essential amino acids.
Cream cheese adds a smooth texture and boosts calcium content.
Dark‑green vegetables are high in lutein and zeaxanthin, antioxidants beneficial for eye health.
Tomatoes provide fresh flavor and are a source of lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
A small amount of added fat (butter or olive oil) helps absorb fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: One serving supplies about 6 g of complete protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B2, B6, and B12 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese and green vegetables increase calcium intake, essential for bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and carotenoids from greens protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from tomatoes and vitamin K from leafy greens help strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume in moderation.

items.title: Sodium and fat
items.content: Cheese and added oil can raise sodium and calorie levels, which should be considered in low‑salt or calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked eggs may harbor Salmonella; cook until fully set.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, garnished with fresh herbs. It works well as a standalone breakfast, as a filling for sandwiches or wraps, or as a side to a vegetable salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat on a skillet or in the microwave to an internal temperature of 75 °C.
